newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour uncertain of outcome of mad cow vote.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour uncertain of outcome of mad cow vote.

text.p: The deputy leader of Britain's opposition Labour party said on Monday he could not be sure whether Labour would defeat the Conservative government in a crucial Parliamentary vote on the mad cow crisis.

Asked whether he expected support from the nine Ulster Unionist MPs who hold the balance in Parliament, John Prescott told reporters, "We will have to wait and see what they are doing. According to the press reports, they are still negotiating.'

Labour has put down a motion on Monday to reduce the salary of agriculture minister Douglas Hogg by one thousand pounds, which would effectively trigger his resignation and a vote of confidence in the government on Tuesday.
Prescott said, "With the Northern Ireland people, they negotiate up to the last minute. Labour's job is to put down this motion of criticism. We have done that and we hope they will back us."
